title: SK Hynix sustains triple-digit YoY revenue growth through Q3 2026
body: SK Hynix reports quarterly, and its next two post-listing results — the Q2 2026 print due in late July and the Q3 2026 print due in October — should extend the run it just posted: first-quarter revenue up nearly 200% year-over-year and a stock up roughly 260% year-to-date on high-bandwidth-memory demand. The prediction is that at least one, and likely both, of those quarters again shows triple-digit (at or above 100%) year-over-year revenue growth. The driver is a memory supply crunch the market has taken to calling 'RAMageddon': AI accelerators consume HBM and DRAM faster than fabs can add capacity, and the capacity the IPO proceeds are earmarked to fund takes roughly two years to come online, so pricing power holds well past the listing. The same scarcity thesis is pulling the whole layer to public markets in one week — SK Hynix's US offering was more than seven times oversubscribed and China's CXMT is following with a roughly 29.5 billion yuan Shanghai listing after 700% year-over-year revenue growth — corroborating evidence that durable demand, not a one-quarter spike, is setting memory prices. The falsifier is base effects: as the 2025 comparison base rises, year-over-year growth naturally compresses, so a sub-100% post-IPO quarter would break the call.

reasoning.because: SK Hynix posted Q1 revenue up ~200% YoY and a ~260% YTD stock gain on HBM demand.
reasoning.given: HBM/DRAM demand outruns fab capacity, and new fabs the IPOs fund take ~2 years to come online.
reasoning.so_that: SK Hynix holds triple-digit YoY revenue growth for at least one more post-IPO quarter as pricing power persists.
reasoning.landing: by Q4 2026, in SK Hynix's next two quarterly earnings reports.
reasoning.plain_language: AI computers use up memory chips faster than factories can make them, so SK Hynix keeps selling out and its sales should stay huge.

summary: SK Hynix's next two post-IPO quarters should again post triple-digit year-over-year revenue growth, as an AI-driven HBM and DRAM supply crunch keeps memory pricing power intact. The record IPO demand for SK Hynix and CXMT signals durable scarcity, not a one-quarter spike.
